hints.title: Write the intersection equation
hints.body: At a meeting point, both expressions for y are equal. Set them equal and collect everything on one side.
hints.recap: Real solutions of the combined equation are intersections of the two graphs.
hints.pitfall: The discriminant of the curve alone does not answer a line-intersection question.
hints.pause: Identify the three coefficients in the resulting quadratic.

recall.reminder: Real solutions of the combined equation are intersections of the two graphs.

hints.title: Allow a touch as well as a crossing
hints.body: Use the discriminant condition for at least one real solution, including a repeated root.
hints.recap: A repeated quadratic root corresponds to touching.
hints.pitfall: Do not use a strict inequality if touching is allowed.
hints.pause: Find and solve the inequality in k, then check its boundaries.

recall.reminder: A repeated quadratic root corresponds to touching.

solution:
Equating y-values gives x2+kx+2=x−2, hence x2+(k−1)x+4=0.

A real intersection exists exactly when D=(k−1)2−16≥0. Thus |k−1|≥4, so k−1≤−4 or k−1≥4.

Therefore k≤−3 or k≥5: E. Equality gives tangency, so both endpoints belong to the answer.
